data.title: Zcash falls 7.34% as its rebound stalls—Can $1,200 hold?
data.description:
Zcash [ZEC] lost 7.34% on October 22, interrupting a recovery that saw it briefly go above the $1,300 price area. At the time of this writing, it was near the $1,225 price level, slightly above the day’s opening level.

The setback puts the $1,200 price area back in focus as futures numbers also decline. All this is coming as developers release software for the planned network upgrade in November, giving holders another development to watch apart from the daily swings.

A setback after a sharp recovery

ZEC had climbed from about $1,100 toward $1,350 before Thursday’s decline of over 7% erased most of that gain.

But despite the loss, the daily chart shows some ground remains below the price. ZEC held above its 50-day price average near the $1,193 price level, while its longer-term averages was considerably lower.

That leaves $1,190–$1,200 as the immediate test for it. If it holds this area, part of the recovery will be preserved. But if it continues to trade below it, it could go down to its recent lows around the $1,100 price area.

Buyers also face a nearby obstacle. Friday’s rise reached around $1,259 before easing, making the $1,240–$1,260 price area the first area to recover and hold. Beyond that, the latest rebound’s peak around the $1,320–$1,360 price area remains a harder challenge.

Futures exposure retreats alongside the price

CoinGlass’s open interest chart shows the dollar value of outstanding ZEC futures contracts falling after a recent jump toward $3 billion.

Its decline can show positions closing, but falling ZEC prices also reduce their dollar value.

November’s upgrade moves a step closer

The Zcash Foundation released Zebra 7.0.0 on October 22, providing stable software support for the forthcoming NU7 upgrade.

Activation is set for block 3,543,405, which is expected to be around November 5. The upgrade targets a reduction in block times from 75 seconds to 25 seconds, which will shorten the expected wait for a first transaction confirmation.

Daily ZEC issuance and the 21 million supply cap remain unchanged.

Final Summary

  • Zcash steadied near $1,225 after Thursday’s 7.34% loss, leaving $1,200 as an immediate test.
  • NU7 software is available ahead of expected November activation, while futures exposure has contracted.

data.title: CoinDCX faces fresh scrutiny over $16M crypto transfers – What happened?
data.description:
Another day, another exploit, and this time CoinDCX, one of the biggest cryptocurrency exchanges in India, is facing scrutiny after suspicious movements involving wallets previously linked to the exchange. According to Darcy (an on-chain investigator), CoinDCX was linked to a suspected $16 million security incident.

On the 21st of October, 2026, approximately 15.99 million USDT and 5,784 TRX were transferred from addresses previously associated with CoinDCX to a single TRON wallet.

In this, the largest transaction involved 15.82 million USDT, after which the funds were split and routed to deposit addresses linked to Binance, OKX, and Gate.

CoinDCX’s co-founder stirs the pot

However, things became heated when CoinDCX co-founder Sumit Gupta denied that the exchange’s active wallets had been compromised. He described the transactions as hackers reusing compromised addresses from the previous incident.

Gupta said,

Thanks for highlighting but this is incorrect and CoinDCX wallets are not breached. Pls don’t spread rumours.

Gupta added,

We have checked all the present CoinDCX central and user addresses. None of them have sent money to these old addresses.

Additionally, co-founder Gupta issued an updated statement explaining that the flagged addresses, including the TQKJQ wallet, had been ‘deprecated’ following the July 2025 exploit.

CoinDCX said it had absorbed the operational losses and credited all affected users. They also noted that their customer assets remained protected in segregated cold storage.

However, blockchain investigator ZachXBT challenged this explanation and presented on-chain evidence for the same.

ZachXBT calls CoinDCX founders ‘clowns’

According to ZachXBT, the address remained active with a liquidity provider, regularly processed user deposits, and interacted with a current CoinDCX hot wallet as recently as April and May 2026.

Remarking on the same, the pseudonymous blockchain investigator added,

Withdraw all funds from CoinDCX if you value your assets. Its co-founders are clowns running a circus.

Naturally, these findings have raised questions on whether the addresses should genuinely be considered inactive. They have also sparked concerns over whether approximately $15.8 million in assets had actually gone missing.

What’s more to this?

Needless to say, this isn’t the first time CoinDCX has been attacked. Back in July 2025, the crypto exchange had already suffered a $44 million hack.

Interestingly, while this CoinDCX exploit was making headlines, SunCrypto, another crypto exchange of India, reported server-side technical issues that have temporarily made its app unavailable.

Now, while its team is working to restore services as soon as possible, the exchange assured users that their funds remain safe and secure.

Final Summary

  • Darcy alleged that CoinDCX was suspected of the transfer of approximately 15.99 million USDT and 5,784 TRX.
  • But CoinDCX co-founder Sumit Gupta rejected claims of the exchange’s active wallets being compromised.

data.title: Blockchain Association urges Congress to ease crypto tax rules for 67M holders
data.description:
In a recent development, the Blockchain Association (BA) has urged the U.S. Congress to introduce clearer and fairer tax rules for cryptocurrencies. They believe that existing regulations create uncertainty and unnecessary compliance burdens for the 67 million Americans who hold and use digital assets.

Therefore, in a letter dated the 22nd of October, 2026, addressed to Senate and House leaders, the industry group outlined its Digital Asset Tax Principles. In fact, they even called for bipartisan legislation that reflects how digital assets function today.

Besides this, the BA also launched TaxClarityforAmerica.com to encourage Americans to contact their elected representatives and support the proposed reforms.

What is the motive behind this?

With this move, the association is seeking a meaningful ‘de minimis’ exemption to simplify taxes on small crypto transactions and cash-like tax treatment for stablecoins. This in turn is intended to reduce reporting requirements potentially.

At the same time, the BA also proposed taxing mining and staking rewards when they are sold or disposed of, rather than when users initially receive them. This is a step that would prevent tax liabilities on rewards that have not been converted into cash.

Additionally, it wants broker reporting requirements to apply only to intermediaries that have custody or control of customer assets. This excludes non-custodial developers and infrastructure providers to protect privacy.

Key recommendation by the Blockchain Association

Another key proposal is to prevent taxes from being triggered when users transfer digital assets between their own wallets, interact with smart contracts, or move assets across blockchains. However, this comes with a condition that their underlying economic ownership remains unchanged.

The association also supports extending wash-sale rules to crypto to prevent investors from claiming artificial losses while ensuring that everyday transactions are not unfairly penalized.

That said, other recommendations include allowing crypto investments in retirement accounts, clarifying staking rules for trusts and investment vehicles. Additionally, permitting mark-to-market accounting for eligible digital assets, simplifying charitable donations of regularly traded cryptocurrencies. It also proposes recognizing blockchain development as eligible research and development activity for tax credits.

The group further advocates a statutory safe harbor for foreign investors trading digital assets on U.S. exchanges. Here, they argue that clearer tax rules could attract liquidity, encourage businesses to remain in the U.S, and prevent innovation from moving offshore.

The unsaid caveat

However, it is important to note that these proposals have not yet been enacted into law.  

Instead, they just represent the Blockchain Association’s recommendations to Congress, and any changes would require legislative action before taking effect.

Still, Coinbase CPO applauded this move when he noted, 

Notably, this coincided with the Blockchain Association (BA) submitting a comment letter to the U.S. Treasury on proposed GENIUS Act regulations, while warning against excessive compliance burdens on crypto firms, exchanges, and DeFi platforms.

Interestingly, all of this follows the U.S. CFTC, led by Chairman Michael Selig, plans to bring more of the crypto market under a unified federal framework after the CLARITY Act failed to advance in September.

Final Summary

  • Blockchain Association outlined its Digital Asset Tax Principles and called for bipartisan legislation. 
  • All the suggestions given by BA are just recommendations to Congress and are not yet accounted for as law.

data.title: Can THIS recent update, hike in network activity sustain PUMP’s price rally?
data.description:
Pump.fun’s token, PUMP, gained traction recently after the platform introduced Pump Bridge as the default route for cross-chain trades, replacing Relay in its app.

According to the reported figures, making Pump Bridge the default cross-chain route could reduce friction for users trading through Pump.fun.  Pump.fun claims that its bridge delivers buys 2x faster, 92% fewer buy errors and better fills than Relay, based on a randomized test within its app.

What’s more intriguing, however, is that on-chain metrics are already reacting to the announcements by showing signs of greater participation.  In fact, the network’s number of active addresses and the number of PUMP holders have both risen lately.

So, can these improvements help sustain the token’s price action?

Active addresses and holder numbers on the rise

According to the recent analysis, the number of active addresses across the network have spiked to new monthly levels over the last few days.

In the last 24 hours alone, the number of active addresses spiked to 89K, hinting at more wallets interacting with the network.

Besides, the number of holders across the network spiked to 462K too, pointing to a broader distribution of PUMP ownership.

Together, these metrics alluded to rising participation around the altcoin. If activity continues to expand after the initial reaction to the bridge announcement, it could help support market interest.

Can PUMP extend its current gains?

Pump Bridge gives Pump.fun a potential catalyst by improving the experience of cross-chain trading. Both the rising number of active addresses and holders could reinforce the positive response if they persist.

However, traders and investors should check whether the recent price gains are accompanied by sustained demand, rather than fading enthusiasm around the announcement.

Final Summary

  • Pump.fun replaced Relay with Pump Bridge as its default cross-chain route.
  • Ntwork’s rising number of active addresses and holder numbers hinted at greater participation around PUMP.

data.title: Bitcoin Open Interest jumps 8% – Why BTC price faces liquidation risks
data.description:
Bitcoin’s [BTC] latest recovery appears increasingly dependent on leveraged Futures buying rather than Spot demand alone. Futures Open Interest (OI) grew 8.04% to $27.12 billion within 24 hours. Despite that, BTC retraced to below $82,000 at press time.

This rise suggests traders are opening new positions to capture further gains, adding momentum to the recovery. However, as seen in prior rallies in August and September, these large increases in OI were followed by sharp declines in price and multiple sell alerts.

Increases in leverage therefore can provide significant impetus to an increase in price. However, they can also make a trader very susceptible to being forced into liquidation at a loss. Since Futures OI is trending back up after a fall-off in October.

Sustained buying could support further gains. Still, if investor sentiment begins to deteriorate, then there could be a cascade of forced liquidations and a larger drop in price.

Altcoins overtake Bitcoin in OI

The dominance of Bitcoin derivatives has weakened significantly as traders continue to use leverage to bet on altcoins. Historically, Bitcoin has held over 90% of all OI. In contrast, currently it accounts for less than half, 42.6%, against altcoins’ 57.4%.

This reversal accelerated from 2022, when the percentage of Bitcoin’s leveraged contracts plummeted and the use of altcoin contracts became much more widespread among large exchange users.

As such, this indicates that there is an opportunity for investment in altcoins beyond Bitcoin. However, this may also mean that the potential for greater losses due to a rapid decline in price for the same altcoins may be dispersed throughout a wider range of assets.

Bitcoin leverage faces liquidation risks

Growing leverage in both Bitcoin and altcoins raises an important issue. Will the leverage currently available in the marketplace be enough to sustain itself?

Although altcoins now represent approximately 57.4% of all OI, it is still too early to determine whether Bitcoin’s current positioning represents an indication. The market will be able to sustain the high level of leverage it is experiencing.

Aggregated Futures OI levels range from $30 billion to $53 billion. Funding Rates have remained steady around +0.004%. As such, there does not appear to be widespread long-side crowding.

Therefore, spot demand will be needed to provide additional support for BTC’s continued growth and will not rely solely on leverage.

Final Summary

data.title: Ethereum’s Glamsterdam testnet hits setback – Why Solana remains ahead
data.description:
Ethereum’s [ETH] main upgrade agenda in 2026 has hit a hiccup. The much-awaited Glamsterdam upgrade, initially scheduled to go live on the Hoodi testnet on the 26th of October, has been cancelled. 

According to security firm Chain Security, the Hoodi testnet was paused after they identified security flaws that have already impacted 13 projects and counting. 

We already found 13 real-world examples and are in responsible disclosure with the affected projects. Please check your contracts as soon as possible, as the EF is determining how many contracts are impacted in which way.

The flaw would make it impossible to retry cancelled transactions. It would also make it easier for attackers to compromise a smart contract with little gas (fee paid to use a network). 

Glamsterdam upgrade seeks to scale Ethereum even further by increasing the block gas limit from 60 million to 200 million and allowing parallel transaction handling. Ideally, the upgrade would make Ethereum high-performance like newer chains such as Solana and Sui. 

The upgrade had a smooth completion in the Sepolia Testnet in early October. This is the first low-risk setup for developers and validator operators to evaluate compatibility. The Hoodi Testnet, which has been paused, acts as the final staged environment before pushing the upgrade to Ethereum mainnet (live network). 

So the security flaw was a great catch before it reached the mainnet. That said, Solana achieved 85x faster transaction finality, further increasing its gap with Ethereum. 

Ethereum vs. Solana: The gap keeps widening

After Solana’s Alpenglow, it is now 57x faster than Ethereum and has 275x more capacity. It’s the capacity bandwidth that Ethereum is trying to resolve by increasing the block gas limit from 60 million to 200 million.  

On transaction finality, it takes Ethereum over 12 minutes to finalize irreversible transactions. For Solana, it now takes 150-200 microseconds, translating to 3,800x faster than Ethereum. 

Collectively, this has allowed Solana to attract 75x more usage, and that’s the gap Ethereum wants to close. In fact, Solana also announced Alpenglow adaptations to usher in its post-quantum plan called Quantumglow. 

Despite the Glamsterdam testnet hiccup, Ethereum is reportedly planning for 4x faster finality. That would mean bringing finality from over 12 minutes to about 3 minutes. It will still be slower compared to Solana’s 0.15 seconds. 

The proposal, also known as Decoupled Consensus, seeks to offer a cleaner pathway to post-quantum signatures and is expected in early 2028. 

Overall, Ethereum is still lagging Solana and needs to fast-track its upgrades as the gap keeps widening. 

Final Summary

  • Ethereum has cancelled the Hoodi testnet activation for Glamderstam upgrade due to security flaws.
  • Ethereum lags behind Solana across finality, capacity, and more as the race for high-performance blockchain intensifies.

data.title: Bitcoin faces quantum risks by 2030 – Can developers secure BTC in time?
data.description:
Conventional asymmetric (public-key) cryptography may become unsafe as early as 2030 due to advances in quantum computing, according to estimates from research and advisory firm Gartner. This was just one among half a dozen other concerns the firm outlined early in 2026.

The list of threats included agentic AI creating new attack surfaces and introducing challenges for traditional identity and access management (IAM).

The clock is ticking for crypto

Most of 2026 is behind us, and the 2030 target might seem quite far away, but in reality it is not. It is not just crypto that faces a post-quantum threat. Individual entities as well as entire sectors, such as banking, need to start thinking about ways to efficiently replace the cryptography embedded in modern technology.

Recently, AMBCrypto reported on the challenges that a quantum-resistant Bitcoin could face. Right now, BIP-360, the network’s quantum-resistant proposal that introduces the new Pay-to-Merkle-Root address type, is only a proposal and isn’t quantum-proof.

The proposal removes the Taproot key-path spending option that exposes the public key on-chain. It solves a particular kind of long-exposure risk, but is not a full solution to quantum risks, nor does BIP-360 migrate existing coins automatically.

The proposal does not offer protection during the window when a transaction is broadcast, exposing the public key before confirmation, the window where the transaction sits in the mempool.

SHRINCS as part of ongoing Bitcoin quantum resistance upgrades

Cryptographic digital schemes that Bitcoin employs right now, ECDSA and Schnorr, have signatures that are very compact. The National Institute of Standards and Technology recommends post-quantum secure hash and lattice-based signature schemes that are 38 to 123 times bigger.

If employed, it would slow the Bitcoin network to a crawl and drop the transactions per second (TPS) to under 1.

A potentially viable alternate signature scheme called SHRINCS was proposed, with a minimum size of 548 bytes that can grow as large as 4,619 bytes.

Unveiled in December 2025, the proposal is a promising research field, but it is not yet cryptographically mature. It has some advantages and trade-offs, for example, the compact signatures, while also introducing a cryptographic state-management problem into every wallet.

A single update is not enough to achieve quantum resistance. Sustained research, engineering efforts, and steady adoption will be needed to strengthen the network.

Final Summary

  • The Bitcoin quantum resistance debate has many questions. The most damaging of them might be the one around whether we have a lot of time to act, or not enough.
  • BIP-360 and SHRINCS are promising proposals that advance the engineering, but the network needs to come to a consensus on which route to go, sooner rather than later.

data.title: UNI price rebounds as Uniswap launches Aggregator Hooks – Is $8 next?
data.description:
Uniswap [UNI] has extended its decentralized trading infrastructure with the launch of Aggregator Hooks, bringing external liquidity into v4 pools across its three networks.

The protocol recently announced that its new upgrade transformed Uniswap v4 into an aggregator, which in turn expanded its liquidity capabilities beyond the conventional pools. The external liquidity sources will be operating within Uniswap’s existing pool infrastructure through Aggregator Hooks, expanding available trading routes.

The feature was launched across Ethereum [ETH], Base, and Robinhood Chain, with access through the Uniswap Web App and API. Notably, the expansion provided developers with additional flexibility while integrating liquidity sources into decentralized trading applications.

This development marked another step in Uniswap’s infrastructure improvement, although the UNI token faced separate concerns around large-holder activity.

Uniswap whale deposit contrasts with spot buying

An OTC-linked wallet reportedly deposited 180,000 UNI, valued around $1.25 million, to Binance, which raised concerns about potential selling pressure. This significant exchange deposit escalated the speculation that the holder could liquidate tokens through the centralized exchange.

Yet, this transaction alone did not, however, establish whether the wallet had executed any sales. In fact, UNI’s Spot Taker CVD remained taker-buy dominant, suggesting stronger aggressive buying activity across the measured period.

Here, this positioning highlighted that the spot buyers maintained an advantage despite the potential supply entering Binance. These diverging developments therefore highlighted a market where buying interest persisted in spite of the uncertainty surrounding whale transactions.

Whether buyers could absorb additional selling remained crucial as Uniswap approached an important technical area.

UNI nears trendline as indicators strengthen

Uniswap’s daily chart highlighted a roughly 3.00% recovery to $7.22, following an extended decline from September highs above $10. The rebound visibly pushed UNI closer to its emerging descending trendline resistance, even though the price was yet to test the boundary.

Supporting the price recovery, the Money Flow Index climbed to 53.45, crossing above its neutral midpoint. Additionally, the RSI indicator improved to 44.67, slightly exceeding its signal average, which sat at 44.13. Even if the indicator remained below the 50-threshold, its improvement suggested easing bearish pressure.

However, for now, the $7.00 level remained crucial support, while a sustained breakout above the descending trendline would validate the bullish bias.

Where could UNI’s liquidity pull price next?

Beyond the daily technical chart, Binance’s 24-hour Liquidation Heatmap revealed considerable liquidity bands on both sides of the prevailing UNI’s price.

Notably, the strongest overhead clusters appeared around $7.25–$7.30, which placed potential short liquidations near UNI’s immediate recovery path. Additional clusters extended towards the $7.40 area, providing another zone of interest in case buyers push through the nearby resistance.

On the other hand, significant downside liquidity visibly accumulated around the $6.85–$6.90 region, which could trigger long liquidations in case of a price correction. These opposing clusters therefore showed potential volatility as the token approached its next directional move.

Overall, the improving technical indicators and dominant spot buying cautiously supported a recovery attempt, although UNI still needed a confirmed trendline breakout.

Final Summary

  • Uniswap introduced Aggregator Hooks across three networks, expanding liquidity access despite potential whale selling.
  • UNI approached descending resistance as improving technical indicators supported a possible breakout toward $8.

data.title: Wormhole crypto falls to $0.0138 – Why bulls face THESE downside risks
data.description:
Wormhole [W] has faced a highly volatile two weeks of trading. Measured from Friday, the 9th of October, to the time of writing, Wormhole crypto prices have faced an 8.21% slide.

During this slide, the altcoin managed to rally 109.78% from $0.0151 to $0.0317, before receding to the current price of $0.0138.

Despite the heavy volatility, the altcoin appeared to hold on to its bullish price structure. There are some levels buyers can keep an eye on, but they also need to be wary of a bearish resumption.

The higher timeframe Wormhole crypto bias

The bearish trend in place for most of 2026 was plotted in yellow. The latest swing high in the downtrend, made in June at $0.0138, was breached in September. This breach of the previous lower high broke the structure and flipped it bullishly.

Since then, the Wormhole crypto price has surged to a new high of $0.0317, a level that the altcoin was last trading at in January 2026.

The surge toward yearly highs and a shift in the price trend was anchored in place by the swing level at $0.0129. The bulls came perilously close to losing this anchor during the recent retracement.

At the time of writing, a daily session close below $0.0129 has not yet occurred. If it does, it would mean that the structure was bearish again.

Swing traders and investors might have to conclude that the recent rally was a liquidity grab, engineered for holders to take profits and exit.

Can W bulls keep the uptrend alive?

The technical indicators on the 1-day chart appeared pessimistic. The OBV took a nosedive after the recent correction and the huge selling volumes after the $0.0317 top was formed.

The RSI on the timeframe also highlighted a bearish bias after it sank below the neutral 50.

The liquidation heatmap drew attention to the nearest magnetic zones swing traders need to watch. A sweep of the $0.0120-$0.0125 area and a bullish price reaction would be an encouraging sight for the bulls.

Meanwhile, a rally into $0.0161-$0.0177 has the potential to face a setback unless heavy spot demand can keep the impulse move going.

Final Summary

  • Wormhole has experienced heavy volatility in the past two weeks, rallying close to 110% in three days before shedding close to 60% over the next eleven days.
  • The $0.0161 and $0.0125 levels of supply and demand would be the next key levels for swing traders to watch.

data.title: Cosmos crypto defies market weakness – Can ATOM rally toward $2?
data.description:
In the past 24 hours, Cosmos [ATOM] has rallied by 3.71%. It was one of only a handful of crypto assets that rallied in the previous day’s trading. CoinMarketCap data showed the altcoin’s daily trading volume spiked 59%.

The market-wide bearish bias was due to Bitcoin’s [BTC] 3% price dip from $84,000 to $81,416 on Thursday, the 22nd of October. ATOM saw a 1.94% price dip on Thursday, alongside the crypto leader, but has enjoyed a more positive Friday at the time of writing.

Can Cosmos crypto’s momentum continue?

From a price structure perspective, the Cosmos 1-day timeframe swing structure has been bearish since October 2025, when the $3.38 low was breached during the brutal sell-off on 10/10.

In hindsight, that was the day crypto markets definitively took a turn toward a bear market. Unfortunately for Cosmos bulls, the altcoin still hasn’t breached this bearish hold.

The $1.21 low and $2.30 high mark the current swing structure. The $2.0 area has been a local supply zone since March 2026, and was briefly flipped to support in May before sellers took control of it in June.

At the time of writing, it is possible that an influx of demand could drive ATOM back to $2.0. The CMF was still below +0.05 to signal no sizeable capital inflows, while the Awesome Oscillator was just below the zero line to signal a pullback was underway.

Signs of hope for ATOM

In the lower timeframes, the bullish momentum has managed to clear the $1.778 local resistance level. A retest of the same could yield another price bounce for ATOM.

Despite the bounce, the CMF remained firmly below +0.05. The daily trading volume hike that CMC data revealed was not enough to sway the technical indicator in the short term.

On the other hand, the Awesome Oscillator has made a bullish crossover back above the zero line.

The 90-day spot taker CVD had been positive in September and October, but has recently taken a neutral turn. A bullish direction reflected in this metric, combined with a steady trading volume increase for ATOM on exchanges, would signal real demand and the possibility of a bullish turnaround.

Final Summary

  • The higher timeframe Cosmos price trend has been bearish since the 10th of October, 2025 selloff.
  • The altcoin was one of only a handful of crypto assets that showed bullish momentum in recent hours, and has managed to overcome the $1.78 local resistance too.
